one_liner: Deprecated wasm-pack build of Rust ed25519-dalek/x25519-dalek for JS; 5.9-7.1x faster than @noble/curves 0.7 on keygen+sign+verify.
what_it_does: Exposes Ed25519 signing (keypair generation, sign, verify) and X25519 key exchange to browsers, Node and Deno by compiling the Rust dalek crates to WebAssembly with wasm-pack and wrapping them in TypeScript classes. The API is object-based, not drop-in for noble: keys, signatures and message buffers are wasm-side objects (Ed25519SigningKey, Ed25519VerifyingKey, Berith.Memory) that must be freed with .free(), `using` or freeNextTick(), and the module must be initialised asynchronously with Berith.initBundledOnce() before first use. The npm package ships the wasm pre-bundled and the build is reproducible in Docker with a CI check against the committed bytecode.
how_it_is_fast: The curve arithmetic runs as compiled Rust in WebAssembly instead of JavaScript BigInt: the benchmarked 1.1.x build used ed25519-dalek 1.0.1 on curve25519-dalek 3.2.1 with the u64_backend (radix-2^51 field elements using native wasm i64 multiplies), whereas @noble/curves 0.7 does field arithmetic on BigInts in V8. Keys stay inside wasm memory between calls in the 'unserialized' mode, so only the 1 KiB message and 64-byte signature cross the JS-wasm boundary. There is no SIMD or hand-written assembly; the gain is compiled fixed-width limb arithmetic versus arbitrary-precision BigInt.
when_to_use: Browser or Deno code that needs Ed25519 signatures or X25519 and has no WebCrypto Ed25519/X25519 it can rely on, where pure-JS noble is the alternative and per-operation latency matters (hundreds of signatures or verifications per second).
Projects pinned to the 1.1.x/1.2.x API that want a reproducible, CI-checked wasm binary rather than a JS implementation.
Workloads that keep long-lived key objects in wasm and sign or verify many messages, which is the 'unserialized' case that produced the 5.85x (Deno) and 7.06x (Node) figures.
Public-domain (Unlicense) licensing is required and a small vendored wasm blob is acceptable.
when_not_to_use: New code: the author deprecated it in favour of @hazae41/ed25519 (pure TypeScript) and @hazae41/ed25519-wasm / @hazae41/x25519-wasm; it gets README edits only since October 2023.

On Node.js: node:crypto (OpenSSL) ran the same keygen+sign+verify loop in 152.67 us versus berith's 281.68 us, and supercop.wasm 5.0.1 ran it in 187.96 us, so berith is the third-fastest option on its own page.
When keys must be serialised on every call (e.g. stored as bytes and reloaded): the serialized variant is about 13% slower and the wasm objects must still be created and freed.

Consensus-critical verification that must match another library bit-for-bit: current noble-curves defaults to permissive ZIP-215 rules (zip215: true), while berith calls ed25519-dalek's default verify (dalek 1.0.1 in the benchmarked build, dalek 2.0.0 now); the two are different rule sets and berith does not document which edge cases it accepts.
X25519-heavy workloads: only Ed25519 was benchmarked; X25519 speed is not documented.

integration.dependencies: @hazae41/box at runtime (HEAD 1.2.6); bundled wasm built from ed25519-dalek 2.0.0, x25519-dalek 2.0.0, wasm-bindgen 0.2.87, getrandom 0.2 (js feature). The benchmarked 1.1.x line bundled ed25519-dalek 1.0.1, x25519-dalek 1.2.0 and rand 0.7.3.
integration.min_toolchain: Using: a JS runtime with WebAssembly and crypto.getRandomValues (browsers, Node, Deno); the README's `using` examples need TypeScript 5.2+ explicit resource management, otherwise call .free(). Building: Rust 1.71.0 (Dockerfile) plus wasm-pack (unpinned) and Node 20.
integration.platforms: Any JS engine with WebAssembly (wasm32); reproducible build documented only on linux/amd64 hosts. Numbers measured on Apple M1 Max with Deno 1.30.3 and Node 18.12.1.
integration.thread_safety: not documented (one wasm instance per JS realm; JS is single-threaded per realm)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same algorithm and wire formats (32-byte keys, 64-byte signatures), but a different object API: inputs must be wrapped in Berith.Memory, results are wasm objects that must be freed, and init is async; noble's functional ed25519.sign/verify calls cannot be swapped in place.

gotchas: The published numbers are for npm 1.1.x (Feb 2023, curve25519-dalek 3.2.1 with u64_backend, opt-level z). The current 1.2.x build uses ed25519-dalek 2.0.0 on curve25519-dalek 4.0.0, whose build.rs picks the 32-bit field backend for wasm32 (the wasm32-to-64-bit override is commented out with 'TODO(Wasm32): Needs tests + benchmarks') and berith sets no curve25519_dalek_bits cfg, so the shipped arithmetic backend differs from the one measured and has never been benchmarked.

The benchmarked 1.1.x line is built on ed25519-dalek 1.0.1, which is affected by RUSTSEC-2022-0093 / CVE-2022-50237 (double public key signing oracle): its Ed25519Keypair.from_bytes accepts a 64-byte secret||public pair and signs with whatever public half is supplied, which leaks the private key if an attacker can choose that half. The 'serialized' benchmark row exercises exactly this from_bytes path. 1.2.0+ (dalek 2.x, 32-byte SigningKey.from_bytes) is not affected; do not use 1.1.x.

Wasm objects are not garbage collected: every key, signature and Memory must be freed or wasm heap memory leaks. The February 2023 bench loop never called .free(), so the measured berith rows excluded deallocation and leaked about three boxed objects per iteration (minor at 300 us per iteration, but not what a correct caller pays).

The deimos benchSync harness has no warm-up and averages all 1,000 performance.now() samples, and its summary prints ratio = other/this, so slower results appear as '0.67x faster' and '0.54x faster'; read those as berith being 1.5x and 1.85x slower than supercop.wasm and node:crypto.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only Ed25519/X25519 signature entry in this category; tape-sha256, sha2-wasm and md5-wasm cover hashing, not signatures. Against its own comparison rows, prefer node:crypto on Node and consider supercop.wasm (faster in the same table) or the author's successor @hazae41/ed25519-wasm for new browser code.
verified_claims_summary: On an Apple M1 Max, a loop of random Ed25519 keypair generation, public-key derivation, signing a 1 KiB message and verifying it took 325.78 us per iteration in Deno 1.30.3 versus 1.9 ms for @noble/curves 0.7.0 (5.85x), and 281.68 us versus 1.99 ms for noble 0.7.1 in Node 18.12.1 (7.06x), with berith built from Rust 1.64.0 via wasm-pack at opt-level z with LTO. The same Node table shows supercop.wasm 5.0.1 at 187.96 us and node:crypto at 152.67 us, both faster than berith; noble-curves' current README (Apple M4, a newer CPU and much newer noble) lists 137 + 283 + 665 us for getPublicKey, sign and verify, so the gap to today's noble is likely smaller than the 2023 ratio, though no run compares them directly.
status_note: Deprecated by its author and stale (code unchanged since npm 1.2.6 in October 2023, README edits through 2025-05-25, 7 stars, no issues); Unlicense makes it free to vendor, but use 1.2.x only, since the benchmarked 1.1.x line sits on the RUSTSEC-2022-0093-affected ed25519-dalek 1.0.1, and the shipped 1.2.x build has never been benchmarked.
